bullets.title: NVDA: Earnings tonight amid CEO departure, export controls, and UBS PT cut to $240
bullets.body: UBS cut NVDA PT from $300 to $240, trimming CY28 revenue from $985B to $885B and EPS from $22.08 to $20.01, citing new BIS rules restricting China remote access to US AI chips (~10% demand headwind, 1-2GW at risk). Options pricing an ~8% implied move on tonight's print (5PM call); market expects a beat to ~$111-112B in FQ3 and FQ4 guide of ~$130B vs. $125B consensus, but soft 71-72% gross margins and cautious 2028+ guidance under interim CEO Colette Kress are the key overhang. SemiAnalysis cut 2028-30 AI accelerator spend by 28-41%, allocating most downside to NVDA; Morgan Stanley removed NVDA from Top Pick status citing CEO succession uncertainty.

bullets.title: NVDA export control fallout: optical/networking stocks surge 5-10% premarket
bullets.body: Trump administration advancing ban on Chinese optical transceiver imports for data centers; COHR +9.3%, FN +7.7%, LITE +5.2%, CIEN +4.8%, ALAB +4.7%, CRDO +4.5%, MRVL +4.3%, TSEM +4.0%, MTSI +3.0%, GLW +2.6% in premarket. Roth QSG survey assessing whether NVDA's 1.6T shipments are cannibalizing 800G among vendors including ANET, AVGO, MRVL, CRDO, CIEN, GLW, FN, COHR, LITE.

bullets.title: NVDA: Citi says AI memory demand concerns overdone; only 12% DRAM/7% NAND at risk
bullets.body: Citi estimates only ~12% of total DRAM and ~7% of NAND demand is exposed to downside even under a severe scenario where NVDA financing halts entirely. NVDA-related financing represents ~14% of total hyperscaler capex; China-located fabs (~24% DRAM, ~31% NAND capacity) face tighter US equipment restrictions, posing a supply rather than demand risk. HBM demand downside seen as limited given robust ASIC-led demand and tight capacity constraints.

bullets.title: DIS: Q4 beats across the board; FY27 double-digit EPS guide, dividend +33%, $9B buyback
bullets.body: DIS Q4 EPS $1.77 beat consensus $1.67; revenue $25.95B beat $25.16B; FCF $4.84B beat $4.39B. FY27 adj. EPS guided to double-digit growth vs. Street +8.5%; Q1 segment OI guidance $5.4B vs. $5.24B consensus; dividend raised 33% to $2.00/share with $9B in planned FY27 buybacks and $3B annual run-rate cost savings target by FY29. Stock -1.6-1.8% in premarket despite the beat, likely reflecting consensus already elevated. Citi maintains Buy at $140 PT; Wolfe maintains Outperform.

bullets.title: CSCO: Double upgrade from DZ Bank and HSBC; PTs $125 and $133 respectively
bullets.body: DZ Bank upgraded CSCO to Buy from Hold (PT $125 from $124, implying 32% upside) and HSBC upgraded to Buy from Hold (PT $133 from $120, implying 41% upside) on the same morning. FactSet consensus PT is $132.

bullets.title: META/AMZN/GOOGL: UBS analyst Keirstead assumes coverage with reduced PTs
bullets.body: New UBS Internet analyst Karl Keirstead assumes: AMZN Buy at $340 (from $352, 32% upside vs. FactSet $327); META Buy at $815 (from $892, 30% upside vs. FactSet $849); GOOGL Neutral at $320 (from $380, 14% upside vs. FactSet $392). All PTs trimmed modestly from prior levels.

bullets.title: ORCL/DELL: Citi flags elevated vol; rates ORCL top AI Defense buy, DELL constructive on AI infra
bullets.body: ORCL down 9% MTD; Citi analyst Radke rates it a top buy among AI Defense names, arguing Democrat-win market reaction overstates fundamental risk and existing cloud/network capacity owners could benefit if new capacity becomes difficult to build. ORCL 1M implied vol at 71.1 (put-call skew at 81st percentile). DELL down 7% w/w with 1M implied vol at 99th percentile (94.6); Citi Hardware analyst Merchant constructive citing AI server/storage strength offsetting weak PC demand.

bullets.title: AAPL: Long-term Samsung DRAM supply deal imminent; MS smartphone survey negative for Android
bullets.body: Apple is finalizing a 4-5 year DRAM LTA with Samsung starting H1/27, including a volume floor at market-based pricing — the last major tech company to sign such an agreement per Maeil. Separately, Morgan Stanley's global smartphone survey cuts CY27 shipments to -5% YoY (bear -11%), with Android declining 9% while iPhone grows 7%; Apple is the only major OEM with positive and improving net switching rates. MS maintains AAPL OW at $350 PT.

bullets.title: AMZN: Ohio $17B data center bet threatened by voter-approved ballot measures
bullets.body: Three Amazon data center projects in Ohio are impacted by 21 voter-approved ballot measures restricting AI infrastructure development. Separately, BXDC acquired Amazon data centers across two campuses for $5B at a 7% cash cap rate (8.1% GAAP), validated by Roth's 6.98% methodology, with a 2.75% annual escalator and 12-year initial term extendable to 32 years.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Geothermal power deal ($500M, 50MW+ from Quaise Energy in Oregon)
bullets.body: Google entered a $500M+ deal to purchase geothermal power from Quaise Energy for a project in Oregon, securing more than 50MW of capacity. This is a data-point for GOOGL's ongoing clean energy strategy for AI infrastructure.

bullets.title: CRM: JPM OW maintained; Agentforce in production but AI monetization gradual, 12-18 month ramp
bullets.body: JPM maintains CRM Overweight; partner surveys show 30-60% of Agentforce clients in production but many have limited usage; 80-90% of projects require substantial data cleanup. ~25% of renewals involve 5-10% seat-reduction requests; Agentforce/Data 360 attach could support 5-10% net TCV expansion but consumption may take 12-18 months to ramp. Core CRM franchise remains durable with high switching costs.

bullets.title: WDAY: JPM OW; F3Q27 expected in-line, GRR recovery at 97% is key investor watchpoint
bullets.body: JPM models F3Q27 subscription revenue $2.52B (+12.1% y/y) in line with guidance; total revenue ~$2.69B, operating margins ~30%. $600M of AI ARR with 12% average ARR uplift from Agentic AI SKUs; FY28 framework of 11% subscription growth carries upside from AI and Flex Credits. WDAY shares at 11x EV/uFCF pricing in continued moderation; stable growth outlook key to addressing conservative expectations.

bullets.title: HOOD: Mizuho OW at $130 PT; wealth-creation roadmap via banking, retirement ($35B+), agentic trading
bullets.body: Post CEO/CFO meeting, Mizuho (OW, $130 PT) highlights: retirement assets over $35B with negative churn; Gold Card at 1.3M cardholders but not broadly available; agentic trading at 200K accounts with early engagement; prediction markets at 30% non-sports volume (up from 15% in Q2). Management does not view Kalshi's equities entry as strategic threat.

bullets.title: CHTR/CMCSA/VZ/T: SpaceX/EchoStar spectrum deal likely if DISH mediation progresses Nov 18
bullets.body: MS/Farrar analysis: SpaceX needs EchoStar's AWS-3 spectrum (~$8.5B value) for competitive terrestrial 5G; DISH bankruptcy mediation conclusion Nov 18 is a key catalyst. Farrar forecasts Starlink at <5% mobile market share by 2031 (not existential for Big 3) but ~10% broadband share within 5 years. SpaceX/cable partnership could strengthen Starlink bundle but creates convergence risk for cable operators.

bullets.title: PENN: Hedgeye adds as new long idea at $17.78; presentation Wednesday
bullets.body: Hedgeye analyst Sean Jenkins initiated PENN Entertainment as a new long idea at $17.78, with a presentation scheduled Wednesday November 18.

bullets.title: MSFT: July software flaw triggered cascading Outlook/Teams outage; reduced by Pershing Square -35%
bullets.body: A Microsoft software flaw undetected since July triggered a cascading outage affecting Outlook and Teams. Separately, Pershing Square reduced its MSFT stake by 35% to 4.1M shares while increasing NFLX by 18% to 15.4M shares. MSFT down 5% w/w in the broader AI selloff.

bullets.title: DELL/HPE/INTU/BABA: Upcoming earnings catalysts this week and next
bullets.body: Key upcoming prints: INTU Thu Nov 19 (EPS est. $2.46, rev $4.30B); HPE Mon Nov 23 (EPS est. $1.27, rev $14.35B); DELL Tue Nov 24 (EPS est. $6.59, rev $49.22B); BABA Thu Nov 19 (rev est. CNY270.1B); WDAY Tue Nov 24 (EPS est. $2.75, rev $2.69B).

bullets.title: AVGO/AMD/MU: SemiAnalysis cuts 2028-30 AI accelerator spend 28-41%; AVGO far less affected than NVDA
bullets.body: SemiAnalysis removes ~$1.6T from cumulative 2027-30 AI accelerator spend. NVDA compute revenue cut 22-66% for 2027-30 with lower Feynman pricing pressure; Broadcom (AVGO) described as far less affected as spend shifts to ASICs. SK Hynix (HBM supplier) benefits from 65% of shipments going to non-NVDA customers (GOOGL, AMZN, AMD). NAND spot prices fell 20% in 2 weeks on weak consumer demand and YMTC competition.

bullets.title: TMUS: Citi raises PT to $185; cost efficiency $1.4B target and SpaceX optionality cited
bullets.body: Citi raised TMUS target price to $185, citing sentiment improvement, stabilizing competitive wireless dynamics, and SpaceX optionality (potential builder or Telco buyer). T-Mobile's $1.4B cost efficiency target for 2027 expected to support margin expansion; postpaid growth algorithm more balanced with price and quantity both contributing.

bullets.title: RBLX/SHOP/ADBE/HUBS/CRM: SaaS cohort becoming 'funding shorts' as Anthropic IPO approaches
bullets.body: OPCO desk flags the SaaS cohort (CRM, HUBS, ADBE, SHOP, RBLX et al.) as funding shorts as Anthropic comes to market. Separately, Wolfe All-SaaS multiples down 3.57% w/w and All-Security multiples down 7.49% w/w; IGV -9.5% YTD vs. S&P +10.5%.
